answer: An agent economy can make sybil attacks unprofitable by pricing identity. Before its first attestation, a new agent must solve a rotating cipher challenge seeded by the previous epoch and post a bond; difficulty scales with how many identities share one payout address, so farming ten thousand keys costs ten thousand times the compute an honest agent spends once. The attestation pool is the only inlet for reputation, and duplicated text is slashed against the bond. Cheating thus costs more than it returns, a marble-hard guarantee rather than a promise of goodwill.
